problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Constrained monotone variational inequality: find xstar ∈ X satisfying ⟨F(xstar), w − xstar⟩ ≥ 0 for every w ∈ X. X is convex; F is continuous and globally monotone. No objective function, strong monotonicity, or saddle representation is assumed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns an exact Euclidean metric projection P(z) onto X, characterized by P(z) ∈ X and ⟨z − P(z), w − P(z)⟩ ≤ 0 for every w ∈ X. Operator evaluations and projections have separate fixed call budgets.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: spec.admissible, second conjunct; LongTails/Template.lean: execute and Convergence.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns the exact operator value F(x) at any ambient-space query x. Answers are independent of the call index and seed; F need not be a gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: L0 > 0 and L1 ≥ 0. For every x, y and M, a bound ‖F(x + θ(y − x))‖ ≤ M throughout θ ∈ [0,1] implies ‖F(x) − F(y)‖ ≤ (L0 + L1 M)‖x − y‖. This is norm-dependent segment smoothness, with no global Lipschitz constant assumed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: spec.valid and segment-bound conjunct of spec.admissible.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is an arbitrary real inner-product space; completeness and finite dimension are not assumed. Public information consists of E, L0, L1, and feasible x0. Hidden budget parameters satisfy R > 0, G ≥ 0, G0 ≥ 0, ε > 0; some VI solution obeys ‖x0 − xstar‖ ≤ R and ‖F(xstar)‖ ≤ G, while ‖F(x0)‖ ≤ G0. X need not be bounded.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/ConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: Public, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and final conjuncts of spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.makeAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The returned point must belong to X.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: Feasibility and the ε residual certificate must hold almost surely under the joint algorithm-seed and oracle-seed probability law.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The returned point x admits a normal-cone certificate ξ with ⟨ξ, w − x⟩ ≤ 0 for all w ∈ X and ‖F(x) + ξ‖ ≤ ε. The criterion is an unsquared norm residual for F + N_X, rather than a VI gap or the norm of F alone.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The monotone VI formulation and exact projection oracle are established, but norm-dependent segment smoothness, hidden solution-scale bounds, and an almost-sure normal-cone residual guarantee form a meaningful variant of the usual globally Lipschitz VI benchmark.
